question.problem:
In $△LMN,$ we have $m∠N={36}^{∘},$ $MN=9,$ and $LM=6.$ Which of the following statements *could* be true?

I. $∠L$ is acute

II. $m∠L={75.02}^{∘}$ rounded to $2$ decimal places

III. $m∠L={61.85}^{∘}$ rounded to $2$ decimal places
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/4f5aad8cf0a25781bc08d6ee51b739ecd68f9d2d7a5acc84230ff743739ea533.png)

The law of sines states that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡L}{l}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡N}{n}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
n=6,\,m∠N={36}^{∘},\,l=9,
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡L}{9} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{36}^{∘}}{6} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡L & =9\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{36}^{∘}}{6} \\  & ≈9\cdot \frac{0.587\,79}{6} \\  & ≈0.881\,69,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠L & ≈\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.881\,69)≈{61.85}^{∘},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠M & ={180}^{∘}-m∠N-m∠L \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{36}^{∘}-{61.85}^{∘} \\  & ≈{82.15}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

However, another solution to $\operatorname{sin}⁡L=0.881\,69$ is given by

$$
m∠L≈{180}^{∘}-{61.85}^{∘}={118.15}^{∘}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠M & ={180}^{∘}-m∠N-m∠L \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{36}^{∘}-{118.15}^{∘} \\  & ≈{25.85}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, there are two possible triangles, with the following angle measures:

- $m∠L≈{61.85}^{∘},\,m∠M≈{82.15}^{∘},\,m∠N={36}^{∘}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/31d18e2602d9acceccea6a0fe672b4c3f992b12c30c4921b3234e2f22cc454af.png)

- $m∠L≈{118.15}^{∘},\,m∠M≈{25.85}^{∘},\,m∠N={36}^{∘}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/b51c7e3eada7a8e44b0fb9912b95684d77b40e49f8c6bde7859e73f20c6d9f40.png)

In conclusion, the correct answer is "I and III only."
